title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #09
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #09 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the columns :
(a)
Robert Burton
(i)
Urn Burial
(b)
Richard ooker
(ii)
The Unfortunate Traveller
(c)
Thomas Browne
(iii)
The Anatomy of Melancholy
(d)
Thomas Nashe
(iv)
Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Politie
(a)
(b)
(c)
(d)
items.explanation: Robert Burton authored The Anatomy of Melancholy (1621) (iii); Richard Hooker wrote Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Politie (1594) (iv); Sir Thomas Browne wrote Hydriotaphia, Urn Burial (1658) (i); and Thomas Nashe authored the picaresque romance The Unfortunate Traveller (1594) (ii).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q2
items.stem:
What do the prosodic features of a
language tell us ?
options: The speaker's native language and its cognate languages
The speaker's age, emotional state, social class, educational background, geographical provenance etc
The speaker's self-confidence or lack of it
The speaker's command of the resources of the language spoken by him/her and their deployment
items.explanation: Prosodic (suprasegmental) features of language—such as intonation, pitch, stress, rhythm, tempo, and voice quality—reveal indexical and paralinguistic details about a speaker's emotional state, age, social class, education, and regional background.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q3
items.stem:
Globalization is antithetical to :
(A) The movement of capital
(B) The movement of commodities
(C) Cultural nationalism
(D) People
(E) Narcissism
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: While globalization accelerates transnational flows of capital and commodities, it is antithetical to insular cultural nationalism (C) and inward-looking narcissism (E), making (C) and (E) Only correct.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q4
items.stem:
Which of the statements given below are true?
A. The centre for contemporary Cultural Studies was established in Berkley in 1960.
B. Jurgen Habermas traces the rise of the public sphere to the rise of print culture.
C. Paul Gilroy introduced the concept of the Black Atlantic.
D. Adorno praises the alien nature of avant-garde modernist art such as the atonal music of Schoenberg.
E. Chutnification was a term used by Edward Soja.
items.explanation: Statements B, C, and D are true: Jürgen Habermas linked the emergence of the bourgeois public sphere to print capitalism and periodicals; Paul Gilroy theorized the "Black Atlantic" (1993); and Theodor Adorno praised Arnold Schoenberg's difficult atonal compositions for resisting culture-industry commodification. Statement A is false because the Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies (CCCS) was founded in 1964 at the University of Birmingham, and statement E is false because "chutnification" is a term coined by Salman Rushdie in Midnight's Children (1981).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q5
items.stem:
Arrange in chronological order the publication of the following anthologies of poetry by Nissim Ezekiel:

A. The Exact Name
B. Latter-Day Psalms
C. Sixty Poems
D. The Unfinished Man
E. A Time to Change

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B, C, D, A and E
E, C, D, A and B
D, E, C, B and A
A, D, B, E and C
items.explanation: Nissim Ezekiel's poetry collections appeared chronologically as follows: A Time to Change (1952, E), Sixty Poems (1953, C), The Unfinished Man (1960, D), The Exact Name (1965, A), and Latter-Day Psalms (1982, B).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q6
items.stem: Who said about Northrop Frye that he did not lock literature into an ivory tower; instead he emphasized its centrality to the development of a civilized humane society?
items.explanation: Canadian author Margaret Atwood, who was taught by Northrop Frye at Victoria College in the University of Toronto, remarked that Frye never locked literature into an ivory tower, but instead affirmed its indispensable place in human social life and democratic culture.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: Michel de Montaigne established the term 'essay' as a new literary form in his text Essays.

Reason R: Francis Bacon is generally considered as the father of English essay.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Ais true but R is false
Ais false but R is true
items.explanation: French Renaissance thinker Michel de Montaigne established the essay as a new genre of personal enquiry with his Essais in 1580 (Assertion A is true), and Francis Bacon introduced the form into English literature with his Essays in 1597 (Reason R is true). However, Bacon's later English works do not explain why Montaigne originated the genre in France.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q8
items.stem: Hudibras of Samuel Butler reflects on the revolt against:
items.explanation: Samuel Butler's mock-heroic verse satire Hudibras (published in three parts in 1663, 1664, and 1678) ridicules the hypocrisy, fanaticism, and pedantry of English Puritans and Presbyterians following the Restoration.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q9
items.stem:
Which of the following describes Foucault's views on knowledge?
(a) Knowledge is not metaphysical or transcendental.
(b) Knowledge is not a matter of perspective.
(c) Knowledge is not pure or neutral but is always from a point of view.
(d) Knowledge is unconstrained by regimes of power.
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: Drawing on Friedrich Nietzsche's genealogy, Michel Foucault argues that knowledge is neither metaphysical nor transcendental (a), and that it is never pure or neutral but always situated within historical power relations and specific perspectives (c).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q10
items.stem: 'Homonyms' are words that _______
options: are pronounced differently but have the same meaning
refer to both the male and female of the human species
refer to people who live in houses with similar structures
are spelt similarly but have different meanings
items.explanation: Homographs (literally 'same writing') are words that share the exact same spelling but have different meanings and origins, and may or may not have different pronunciations—such as 'lead' (the metal) and 'lead' (to guide), or 'bank' (financial institution vs. river edge).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q11
items.stem:
Which of these does the book How to read Donald Duck identify as an important element in its analysis of
imperialist ideology in the Walt Disney comicbook?
items.explanation: In How to Read Donald Duck: Imperialist Ideology in the Disney Comic (1971), Ariel Dorfman and Armand Mattelart critique how Disney comics portray Third World indigenous peoples as childlike 'noble savages' who happily surrender their natural wealth to Western capitalists.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q12
items.stem:
Two of the following plays won the Sultan Padamsee Prize for Indian plays in English :

I.
Princes

II.
Where There's a Will

III.
Larins Sahib

IV. Doongaji House

The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: The prestigious Sultan Padamsee Award for Indian plays in English was won by Gurcharan Das's historical play Larins Sahib (in 1968) and Cyrus Mistry's Parsi drama Doongaji House (in 1978), making III and IV the correct combination.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q13
items.stem:
Which among the following is correct in the context of R. K. Narayan?
A. His The Guide is an open-ended novel.
B. Most of the characters of his novels are from elite section of society.
C. He wrote a short story titled "The Martyr's Corner."
D. He received the Booker's prize for his novel The Vendor of Sweets.
E. Malgudi is a real-life city in Karnataka.
Choose the correct option given below:
items.explanation: R.K. Narayan's Sahitya Akademi Award-winning novel The Guide (1958) has a famously open-ended conclusion as Raju collapses while fasting for rain (A), and Narayan wrote the classic short story 'The Martyr's Corner' (C). Malgudi is a fictional town, his characters are middle- and lower-middle-class, and he never won the Booker Prize.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q14
items.stem: Which post-War British poet ends a poem with the line, “Get Stewed : Books are a load of crap” ?
items.explanation: The line closes Larkin's 'A Study of Reading Habits' (1964).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q15
items.stem:
Sequence the following works of Dostoyevsky in the order of their publication:
A. Notes from Underground
B. Crime and Punishment
C. The Idiot
D. The Brothers Karamazov
E. Poor Folk
items.explanation: Fyodor Dostoevsky's major works appeared in the following chronological order: Poor Folk (1846, E), Notes from Underground (1864, A), Crime and Punishment (1866, B), The Idiot (1869, C), and The Brothers Karamazov (1880, D), establishing E-A-B-C-D.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q16
items.stem:
Which novel of Toni Morrison tells the wrenching story of a protagonist who murders her
child rather than to allow him/her to live as a slave ?
items.explanation: Toni Morrison's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel Beloved (1987)—inspired by the life of enslaved fugitive Margaret Garner—tells the story of Sethe, who kills her two-year-old daughter rather than allow slave catchers to return her to slavery at Sweet Home.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q17
items.stem:
Identify the name of the essayist who made the following assertion:
“If a man will begin with certainties, he shall end in doubts, but if will be content to begin with doubts, he shall end in certainties.”
items.explanation: Sir Francis Bacon wrote this aphorism in Book I of The Advancement of Learning (1605), arguing that genuine philosophical and scientific discovery begins with rigorous doubt and methodical inquiry rather than unquestioned dogmas.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q18
items.stem: Who said that an author has no claim to original thought but only to apt presentation of what was already being thought by others?
items.explanation: Alexander Pope famously expressed this neoclassical view in An Essay on Criticism (1711): 'True Wit is Nature to advantage dress'd, / What oft was thought, but ne'er so well express'd,' arguing that poetic excellence lies in giving ideal form to universal truths.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q19
items.stem:
Which of the following poems are by Sir Walter Scott ?
(A) "Christmas in the Olden Time"
(B) "After the Last Breath"
(C) "Lochinvar"
(D) "Dance of Death"
(E) "A Man was Drawing near to Me"
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Sir Walter Scott wrote 'Christmas in the Olden Time' (from Marmion, 1808, A), 'Lochinvar' (also from Marmion, C), and 'The Dance of Death' (1815, D), whereas 'After the Last Breath' and 'A Man Was Drawing Near to Me' are poems by Thomas Hardy; thus Option 4: (A), (C) and (D) Only.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q20
items.stem:
"To tell the truth Shug act more manly
than rest, men. I mean she upright,
honest, speak her mind…"

What light does the quotation throw
on Shug Avery ?
options: She is upright and honest in asserting her lesbian identity
items.explanation: Spoken by Celie in Alice Walker's epistolary novel The Color Purple (1982), this remark highlights how the independent blues singer Shug Avery subverts conventional gender roles through her bold self-assertion and her honest, unashamed embrace of her lesbian/bisexual identity (Both B and C).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I
List - II
(I) David Malouf
(a) The Solid
Mandala
(II) Patrick White
(b) Wild Cat Falling
(III) Peter Carey
(c) Remembering
Babylon
(IV) Colin Johnson
(d) True History of
the Kelly Gang

(I)
(II) (III) (IV)
items.explanation: These Australian authors match with their novels as follows: David Malouf wrote Remembering Babylon (1993, I-c), Patrick White wrote The Solid Mandala (1966, II-a), Peter Carey wrote True History of the Kelly Gang (2000, III-d), and Indigenous Australian writer Colin Johnson (Mudrooroo) wrote Wild Cat Falling (1965, IV-b).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q22
items.stem:
Who is the author of Mary, and the
unfinished The Wrongs of Woman ?
items.explanation: Feminist philosopher Mary Wollstonecraft wrote the novel Mary: A Fiction (1788) and left behind the unfinished philosophical Gothic novel Maria: or, The Wrongs of Woman, which her husband William Godwin published posthumously in 1798.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q23
items.stem:
Identify the correctly matched group :
(I)
"Because I
could not stop
for death…
(a)
Walt
Whitman
(II) "O Captain !
My Captain!"
(b)
William
Carlos

diverged in a
wood…"

(I)

items.explanation: These celebrated opening lines of American poetry match with their authors as follows: 'Because I could not stop for Death' by Emily Dickinson (I-c), 'O Captain! My Captain!' by Walt Whitman (II-a), 'Two roads diverged in a wood' by Robert Frost (III-d), and 'so much depends / upon' by William Carlos Williams (IV-b).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q24
items.stem:
As mentioned in "My First Acquaintance with Poets" which poet does William Hazlitt describe
as the "only person | ever knew who answered the idea of a man of genius"?
items.explanation: In his autobiographical essay 'My First Acquaintance with Poets' (published in The Liberal in 1823), William Hazlitt recalls hearing Samuel Taylor Coleridge preach at Shrewsbury in January 1798. Hazlitt praises Coleridge's spellbinding eloquence, calling him 'the only person I ever knew who answered to the idea of a man of genius'.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q25
items.stem:
Arrange the following literary texts in the order of their publication :
(A) The Taming of the Shrew
(B) Love's Labour Lost
(C) The Merchant of Venice
(D) Much Ado About Nothing
(E) The Winter's Tale
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Shakespeare wrote these roughly in the order Taming of the Shrew (c. 1591), Love's Labour's Lost (c. 1595), Merchant of Venice (c. 1597), Much Ado (c. 1599) and The Winter's Tale (c. 1610).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q26
items.stem:
Identify the novelist who wrote the following lines; and to whom is it written?
"In delineating male character, I labour under disadvantages; intuition and theory will not adequately supply the place of observation and experience. When I write about women, I am sure of my ground—in the other case I am not so sure."
options: Charlotte Brontë wrote to James Taylor
Jane Austen wrote to Elizabeth Sewell
Margaret Oliphant wrote to Isabella Blackwood
Charlotte Yonge wrote to Felicia Skene
items.explanation: Charlotte Brontë wrote these lines in a letter dated March 1, 1849 to James Taylor of her publishing house Smith, Elder & Co., reflecting on the difficulty of portraying male characters while writing Shirley.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: The technique of art is to make objects "unfamiliar", to make forms difficult, to increase the difficulty and length of perception.
Reason R: The process of perception is an aesthetic end in itself and must be prolonged.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
items.explanation: In his Russian Formalist essay 'Art as Technique' (1917), Viktor Shklovsky defines defamiliarization (ostranenie) by stating that art makes objects unfamiliar and increases the difficulty and length of perception because the perceptual process is an aesthetic end in itself.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q28
items.stem: Kipling’s story “Mrs Bathurst” is set in
items.explanation: Rudyard Kipling's enigmatic modernist short story 'Mrs Bathurst' (collected in *Traffics and Discoveries*, 1904) is set in South Africa, taking place at a railway siding near Simon's Town on the Cape Peninsula.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following are written by William Faulkner?
A. Sanctuary
B. Color Struck
C. Jesus, The Son of Man
D. Light in August
E. Absalom, Absalom!
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Sanctuary (1931, A), Light in August (1932, D), and Absalom, Absalom! (1936, E) are modernist Southern Gothic novels written by William Faulkner. Color Struck (1925) is a play by Zora Neale Hurston, and Jesus, the Son of Man (1928) is by Kahlil Gibran.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q30
items.stem: Allan Sealy’s The Trotter-Nama traces the history of the Anglo-Indian community in a chronicle of seven generations of the Trotter family, told by the seventh Trotter. This narrator is
options: an accountant in the Indian army.
a quack in the Indian outback.
items.explanation: The seventh Trotter, Eldon, is a painter who forges Indian miniatures.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the poem with the opening lines :
(a) “Ode to Psyche”  (i) “My heart aches, and a drowsy numbness pains / My sense, as though of hemlock I had drunk,”
(b) “Ode on a Grecian Urn”  (ii) “No, no, go not to Lethe, neither twist / Wolf’s-bane, tight-rooted, for its poisonous wine,”
(c) “Ode to a Nightingale”  (iii) “Thou still unravish’d bride of quietness, / Thou foster-child of silence and slow time,”
(d) “Ode on Melancholy”  (iv) “O Goddess ! hear these tuneless numbers, wrung / By sweet enforcement and remembrance dear,”
items.explanation: 'O Goddess! hear these tuneless numbers' opens Psyche, 'Thou still unravish'd bride' opens the Urn, 'My heart aches' opens the Nightingale, and 'No, no, go not to Lethe' opens Melancholy.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q32
items.stem:
In Practical Criticism I.A. Richards
links four kinds of meanings in most
human utterances to four aspects.
These are
items.explanation: In Practical Criticism (1929), I. A. Richards divides total meaning in human utterances into four distinct functions: Sense (the literal propositional content), Feeling (the speaker's emotional attitude toward the subject), Tone (the speaker's attitude toward the listener), and Intention (the speaker's conscious or unconscious aim).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q33
items.stem:
Which articles of Indian Constitution pertain to the provisions relating to the Official Language of the Union?
A. 342
B. 343
C. 344
D. 345
E. 346
items.explanation: Under Part XVII (Chapter I) of the Indian Constitution, titled "Language of the Union", Article 343 provides for the official language of the Union (Hindi in Devanagari script) and Article 344 provides for the Commission and Committee of Parliament on official language (B and C). Articles 345 and 346 govern regional and inter-state official languages.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q34
items.stem: More's Utopia displays strong influence of I. The Arthurian legends II. Plato's Republic III. Amerigo Vespucci's account of the travels IV. The teachings of John Wycliffe The correct combination according to the code is
items.explanation: Sir Thomas More's Utopia (1516) is directly modeled on the philosophical communism and civic structure of Plato's Republic (II) and framed by the New World travel narratives of Amerigo Vespucci (III), with whom More's narrator Raphael Hythloday is said to have sailed.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q35
items.meta: Unit VI: English in India: History, Evolution and Futures
items.stem:
Arrange the following commissions, committees, and events, which were important in the context of the history of English in India, in chronology:
A. Gokak Committee Report
B. Acharya Ramamurti Commission
C. All India Language Conference
D. Kothari Commission
E. The Official Language Act
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of these language and education policy milestones in India is: the All-India Language Conference (C, 1956), the Official Languages Act (E, 1963), the Kothari Commission (D, 1964–1966), the Gokak Committee Report (A, 1981–1982), and the Acharya Ramamurti Review Committee (B, 1990).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q36
items.stem:
From the statements given below, what is true about the Gothic Novel?
A. It appeared in 14th Century American Literature.
B. It often uses the medieval form of architecture as setting.
C. It is a form of baroque art.
D. It represents a style of mosaic and fresco wall painting.
E. It aims at evoking chilling terror by exploiting mystery and a variety of horrors.
items.explanation: Statements B and E are true: Gothic novels characteristically set their plots in medieval ruins, castles, and monasteries, aiming to evoke terror, dread, and suspense through the supernatural and mysterious. Statement A is false because the Gothic genre began in 18th-century England with Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto (1764), while C and D confuse literary Gothicism with unrelated visual arts.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Unlike scientific research, literary research does not have specific materials for investigation and scientific
tools for reaching a conclusion and formulating a theory.
Statement II: Literary research consists of critical interpretations of an author's work to the exclusion of biography and
editing of texts.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
items.explanation: Both statements are incorrect: literary research employs rigorous textual, archival, and methodological tools to investigate primary and secondary materials, and it encompasses biography, textual scholarship, and scholarly editing alongside critical interpretation.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q38
items.stem:
Which of the following is NOT TRUE of the New Bolt Report, “The Teaching of English in
England” ?
options: It proposed the teaching of English Literature at the university level.
It urged the teaching of the national literature.
It aimed at uniting divided classes after the war.
items.explanation: The Newbolt Report (The Teaching of English in England, 1921), chaired by Sir Henry Newbolt, aimed to unify British social classes through elementary and secondary school literature education rather than emphasizing elite university curricula.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q39
items.stem:
Which three of the following poets figure in William Dunbar's Lament for the Makers?
(a) Geoffrey Chaucer
(b) John Gower
(c) Robert Henryson
(d) William Langland
Choose the most appropriate option :
items.explanation: In his Middle Scots elegy 'Lament for the Makaris' (c. 1505) with its refrain Timor mortis conturbat me, William Dunbar mourns the deaths of Geoffrey Chaucer (a), John Gower (b), and fellow Scottish makar Robert Henryson (c), but does not mention William Langland.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q40
items.stem: Who claimed : "I have not published a single paper that is not written in a spirit of benevolence and with a love of mankind" ?
items.explanation: Joseph Addison made this remark regarding his periodical essays in The Tatler and The Spectator (1711–12), which sought to 'enliven morality with wit, and to temper wit with morality' in a spirit of benevolence rather than harsh personal satire.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q41
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Collocation
B. Inflected
C. Polarity
D. Generative
I. A term borrowed in the 1960s from mathematics into linguistics by Noam Chomsky
II. A term for the contrast between positive and negative in sentences, clauses, and phrases
III. A habitual association between particular words
IV. A term in which a word takes various forms to show its grammatical role
items.explanation: These linguistic concepts match their descriptions: 'Collocation' denotes habitual lexical co-occurrence (A-III), 'Inflected' refers to words taking variable forms to indicate grammatical roles (B-IV), 'Polarity' marks the grammatical contrast between affirmative and negative constructions (C-II), and 'Generative' refers to Noam Chomsky's formal, rule-governed linguistic model (D-I).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q42
items.stem: In which city did John Ruskin see a paradigm for Victorian Britain ?
items.explanation: In his monumental three-volume architectural treatise The Stones of Venice (1851–1853), Victorian critic John Ruskin interpreted the rise and fall of the maritime empire of Venice—from pious Gothic craftsmanship to corrupt Renaissance luxury—as a moral warning and paradigm for industrial Victorian Britain.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q43
items.stem:
Which two of the following novels belong to the Victorian Age in English Literature?
(a) Pendennis
(b) The Way of All Flesh
(c) The Battle of the Books
(d) Barchester Towers
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: William Makepeace Thackeray's Pendennis (a, 1848–1850) and Anthony Trollope's Barchester Towers (d, 1857) were both published during the Victorian era. Jonathan Swift's The Battle of the Books (1704) is Augustan, and Samuel Butler's The Way of All Flesh was published in 1903.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q44
items.stem: The property of research to replicate the same results using the same technique is termed as –
items.explanation: Reliability in research methodology denotes the consistency and repeatability of a measurement technique, ensuring that applying the same procedure under identical conditions repeatedly produces the same results.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the following children's books in the correct chronological order of their publications:
A. J.K. Rowling - The Goblet of Fire
B. Philip Pullman - Northern Lights
C. C.S. Lewis- The Lion, The Witch, and the Wardrobe
D. J.R.R. Tolkien's - The Hobbit
E. William Golding's - Lord of the Flies
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Starting with J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (D, 1937), followed by mid-century classics Lord of the Flies (E, 1954) and The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (C, 1950), Philip Pullman's Northern Lights (B, 1995), and J. K. Rowling's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (A, 2000), Option 1 (D, E, C, B, A) is the only choice matching the 1937 start and 1995–2000 end.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q46
items.stem: From whose work did John Milton take the epigraph to his Areopagitica?
items.explanation: On the title page of Areopagitica (1644), John Milton placed an epigraph from Euripides' tragedy The Suppliants (Hiketides), along with his own verse translation celebrating free speech as the foundation of true liberty.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q47
items.stem:
Which of the following are correct about the components Romantic epistemology ?
(A) The active-projective view of human self or mind
(B) Mechanical, impersonal and artificial
(C) Distrust of reason
(D) Belief in reason
(E) Collectivism
items.explanation: Romantic epistemology is characterized by an active-projective view of the human mind as a creative source of perception (A) and a fundamental distrust of dry Enlightenment rationalism in favor of emotion and imagination (C).

items.title: Mock #09 · Q48
items.stem: Choose from the following options the correct combination of playwrights who contributed to the movement called "Kitchen Sink Drama".
options: John Osborne, Arnold Wesker, Antonin Artaud and John Arden
John Osborne, Arnold Wesker, Harold Pinter and Shelagh Delaney
John Osborne, Arnold Wesker, Shelagh Delaney and John Arden
John Osborne, Harold Pinter, Shelagh Delaney and John Arden
items.explanation: John Osborne (Look Back in Anger), Arnold Wesker (The Wesker Trilogy), Shelagh Delaney (A Taste of Honey), and John Arden (Live Like Pigs) were key British 'Kitchen Sink' social-realist playwrights of the late 1950s, whereas Harold Pinter is associated with the Comedy of Menace and Antonin Artaud with the Theatre of Cruelty.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q49
items.stem:
Who among the following writers were associated to Harlem Renaissance?
A. Leslie Janison
B. Stephen King
C. Alain Locke
D. Langston Hughes
E. Zora Neale Hurston
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Philosopher Alain Locke (editor of The New Negro, 1925, C), poet Langston Hughes (D), and novelist-anthropologist Zora Neale Hurston (E) were leading figures of the 1920s–30s Harlem Renaissance, whereas Leslie Jamison and Stephen King are contemporary American authors; thus C, D, E only.

items.title: Mock #09 · Q50
items.stem: Which of the following is not true of post-structuralism ?
options: It seeks to undermine the idea that meaning pre-exists its linguistic expression
There can be no meaning which is not formulated and no language formulation reaches anywhere beyond language
There is no a-textual 'origin' of a text
Every sign refers to every other sign adequately
items.explanation: Post-structuralism rejects the structuralist view of language as a closed, stable system. Drawing on Jacques Derrida's concept of différance, it holds that meaning is endlessly deferred along a chain of signifiers, so no sign ever refers to every other sign with complete adequacy.

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow:
At school the study of literature can still involve a close reading or 'practical criticism' of a novel, play or poem without much or any recourse to external material. Practical criticism is the method of analysing a poem, in isolation from the circumstances of its production, developed by I. A. Richards (1893–1979) in the 1920s. He felt that concentration upon 'the words on the page', the technical aspects of the ways verse creates effects, would result in meaningful judgements upon whether a poem was intrinsically 'good' or simply reputedly so. The methodology of practical criticism seeks coherence in images, themes and patterns of language. Richards and his colleagues felt that this practice was 'scientific' and led to objective value judgements. He was part of a group of lecturers at Cambridge University who played a crucial role in the development of the discipline of English Literature and whose methodology influenced the critical practices of the New Critics, John Crowe Ransom (1888–1974) and Cleanth Brooks (1906–94) and their colleagues in the US. Their 'scientific' examination of literature asserted a hierarchy of texts, those that held universal meaning and significance through aesthetic form and those deemed too formulaic to warrant academic scrutiny. The first revered group of texts is often referred to as the literary canon.

In the context of the above passage, close reading implies
options: reading a text by adopting an interdisciplinary mode of inquiry.
reading a text by emphasising on its affective capacity.
reading a text by focussing on words and the technical aspects.
reading a text by adopting a phenomenological approach.
items.explanation: As stated in the passage, close reading or practical criticism involves concentrating directly on 'the words on the page' and the technical aspects of how language, imagery, and verse patterns create meaning in isolation from external biographical or historical context.

options: ensure that criticism adopted a practical perspective to life and basic human issues.

"The methodology of practical criticism seeks coherence in images, themes and patterns of language."
What could be the implication of this statement?
options: Practical criticism involves a political hermeneutic.
Practical criticism prioritises on evaluating texts by adopting a purely literary mode of inquiry bereft of contextualization.
Practical criticism privileges a pragmatic approach.
